reason: The text explicitly describes the king and nobles of Nineveh issuing a proclamation (מִטַּעַם הַמֶּלֶךְ וּגְדֹלָיו - 'by the decree of the king and his nobles') commanding a fast and repentance. The people of Nineveh respond collectively by believing God, proclaiming a fast, wearing sackcloth, and turning from their evil ways - notably stated as being 'from the greatest of them to the least of them' (מִגְּדוֹלָם וְעַד־ קְטַנָּֽם), indicating comprehensive participation across all social levels. The passage demonstrates coordinated action where leadership issues direction and the entire population participates in the same religious and moral response.
